prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2001 – Summary (ideological framing preserved)

Core purpose: Freedom, Justice, Honesty. An enabling, less intrusive state guarantees the essentials—good schools and hospitals, safe streets, reliable transport, decent pensions—so everyone can fulfil their potential. Fairness funds freedom, and green principles run through every policy.

Health
- Cut waiting times by expanding NHS capacity: 27,500 more nurses, 4,600 more doctors, 10,250 allied professionals, 10,000 beds; £1,000 annual uplift for the lowest‑paid NHS staff; free personal care for the elderly and long‑term patients.
- Shift to prevention: restore free dental and eye checks, invest in diagnostics and public health, greener homes and cleaner air.
- End the “postcode lottery” via a national Pharmaceutical Agency; establish Patient Care Guarantees, advocates, and no‑fault compensation; ban age discrimination; end mixed wards.
- Free professionals from central diktats.

Education, Skills and Work
- Honest funding: add 1p to the basic income tax rate to invest over £3bn annually.
- Smaller classes and more staff: primary class averages cut to 25; 5,000 extra secondary teachers; 40,000 classroom assistants; paid preparation time; scrap crude performance pay and SATs at 7; cut bureaucracy; richer books/ICT.
- Abolish university tuition fees; restore grants for the poorest; widen access and support staff.
- Lifelong learning entitlements; paid study leave for 16–24s; replace the New Deal with a flexible, universal job‑help guarantee.

Law, Order and Liberty
- 6,000 more police and 2,000 retained community officers; a Community Safety Force for nuisance crime; independent police complaints; evidence‑led “stop and search.”
- Be tough and effective: more prevention, rehabilitation and community sentences; work and skills in prisons; reduce reoffending.
- Uphold rights: victim statements; end blanket mandatory sentences; protect jury trial and right to silence; liberalise licensing; civil penalties, not criminalisation, for TV licence non‑payment.

Transport
- Integrated, affordable, cleaner travel: free off‑peak buses for pensioners/disabled; aim half‑fares for under‑19s; greener VED with no real‑terms fuel duty rise.
- Empower councils (bonds, congestion charging) to fund better buses, trams, cycling and reopened rail.
- Stronger public control: a Sustainable Transport Authority; restructure Railtrack into a public‑interest model; rural transport fund; a 40% cut in road deaths/serious injuries target.

Pensions, Low Pay and Welfare
- Immediate pension boosts (more for over‑75s/80s), funded by a new 50p rate over £100,000; Independent Pensions Authority; toward citizen‑owned second pensions; end punitive means‑testing traps.
- Annual minimum wage review (single adult rate from 16+); extra help for children in long‑term poverty; fairer support for disabled people.

Economy, Business and Consumers
- Competitive, open markets with lighter, smarter regulation; small business rates allowance; tougher action on monopolies and bank practices; stronger consumer protections.
- A green economy: replace Climate Change Levy with a fair carbon tax; at least 10% renewables by 2010; phase out nuclear as plants retire; boost research and innovation; stop public subsidies for arms exports.

Democracy and Rights
- Fair votes: AV+ for Westminster as a first step, STV for local/EU; replace the Lords with an elected Senate; stronger Commons scrutiny and Freedom of Information; devolve more power to nations, regions and councils; local income tax.
- Equality Act covering all forms of discrimination; repeal Section 28; fair, faster asylum with dignity; judicial warrants for surveillance; no ID cards.

Communities, Countryside and Seas
- Brownfield first; recycling to 60%; flood resilience; protect green spaces; support village services; reform CAP/CFP toward sustainability and local co‑management; create a Ministry for Rural Affairs.

Europe, Defence and the World
- Pro‑EU reformer: enlargement, a clear constitution with subsidiarity, transparency; euro entry by referendum at a sustainable rate.
- Ethical internationalism: strengthen UN, ICC and conflict prevention; maintain defence spending with flexible, deployable forces; retain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing global disarmament; oppose US NMD.

Funding honesty: 1p for education; 50p top rate funds pensions/NHS; close CGT loopholes for police/transport; green tax shifts offset by cuts elsewhere; Citizen’s Tax Contract for transparency.
